spots.name: Exeter Cathedral

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Exeter Cathedral, properly known as the Cathedral Church of Saint Peter in Exeter, is an Anglican cathedral, and the seat of the Bishop of Exeter, in the city of Exeter, Devon, in South West England.

photo.author: Rüdiger Wölk This photo was taken by Rüdiger Wölk. Please credit this photo Rüdi

spots.name: Exeter St Davids railway station
spots.summary: Exeter St Davids railway station is the largest and busiest railway station in Exeter, although it is not as convenient for the city centre as Exeter Central railway station.

spots.name: Parliament Street
spots.summary: Parliament Street is a 50-metre (160 ft)-long street in the city Exeter, Devon, England. It links High Street to Waterbeer Street and dates from the 14th century.

spots.name: Rougemont Castle

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Rougemont Castle, also known as Exeter Castle, is the historic castle of the city of Exeter, Devon, England. It was built into the northern corner of the Roman city walls starting in or shortly after the year 1068, following Exeter's rebellion against William the Conqueror.

photo.author: Rougemont_Castle_gatehouse,_2010.jpg: Juan J. Martínez from Exeter, UK derivativ

spots.name: Exeter Cathedral astronomical clock
spots.summary: The Exeter Cathedral Astronomical Clock is a fifteenth-century astronomical clock in Exeter Cathedral, England. It displays the hour of the day, the day of the lunar month and the phase of the moon. The modern clock mechanism was installed in 1885 by Gillett & Bland of Croydon, and restored in 1910.

spots.name: Royal Albert Memorial Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Royal Albert Memorial Museum & Art Gallery (RAMM) is a museum and art gallery in Exeter, Devon, the largest in the city. It holds significant and diverse collections in areas such as zoology, anthropology, fine art, local and foreign archaeology and geology.

spots.name: Isca Dumnoniorum

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Isca Dumnoniorum, also known simply as Isca, was originally a Roman legionary fortress for the Second Augustan Legion in the Roman province of Britannia at the site of present-day Exeter in Devon.

spots.name: Devon County War Memorial
spots.summary: The Devon County War Memorial is a First World War memorial, designed by Sir Edwin Lutyens and situated on Cathedral Green in Exeter, the county town of Devon, in the south west of England.

spots.name: 24, West Street
spots.summary: The House That Moved is a historic building in Exeter, originally built in the late Middle Ages and relocated in 1961 when the entire street it was on was demolished to make way for a new bypass road linked to the replacement of the city's bridge over the River Exe.

spots.name: Exeter Guildhall
spots.summary: Exeter Guildhall on the High Street of Exeter, Devon, England has been the centre of civic government for the city for at least 600 years. Much of the fabric of the building is medieval, though the elaborate frontage was added in the 1590s and the interior was extensively restored in the 19th century.

spots.name: Old Exe Bridge

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Old Exe Bridge is a ruined medieval bridge in Exeter in south-western England. Construction of the bridge began in 1190, and was completed by 1214. The bridge is the oldest surviving bridge of its size in England and the oldest bridge in Britain with a chapel still on it.

spots.name: St. Mary Major

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of St Mary Major, formerly Exeter Minster, was a historic church and parish in the City of Exeter, Devon, dating from the 7th century. It pre-dated the first Exeter Cathedral by some five centuries, was rebuilt several times, but was finally demolished in 1971.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Church of St Mary Major, Exeter

spots.name: St Martin's Church
spots.summary: St Martin's Church in Cathedral Close, Exeter, Devon, England was built in the 15th century. It is recorded in the National Heritage List for England as a designated Grade I listed building, and is now a redundant church in the care of the Churches Conservation Trust. It was vested in the Trust on 1 August 1995.

spots.name: Church of St Mary Steps

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of St Mary Steps is a Grade I Listed church in the city of Exeter, England.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Church of St Mary Steps, Exeter

spots.name: Exeter city walls

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Exeter's city walls survive as a circuit approximately 2.35km long, of which 72% (1,705m) is still visible, some parts up to 2.5m high. The walls of Exeter, England, are a scheduled monument.

spots.name: Cathedral Close
spots.summary: The area of Cathedral Close, Exeter has been in the centre of Exeter, Devon, England, since Roman times when there was a basilica and a bath house in this area. A church was established here by the seventh century when a young Saint Boniface came from Crediton to study.

spots.name: Mol's Coffee House
spots.summary: Mol's Coffee House is a historic building and coffeehouse in Exeter, Devon. It is a Grade I Listed building. The house is in the northern corner of Cathedral Close, adjoining Cathedral Yard and overlooking Cathedral Green and the North tower of the Cathedral. It is alongside St Martin's Church.

spots.name: Sacred Heart Church, Exeter

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Sacred Heart Church is a Roman Catholic Parish church in Exeter, Devon, England. It is a part of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Plymouth. It was built from 1883 to 1884 and designed by Leonard Stokes. It is situated on the corner of South Street and Bear Street, close to Exeter Cathedral in the centre of the city.

spots.name: St Nicholas Priory

hours.note: Closed Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri, Sat

spots.summary: The Benedictine Priory of St Nicholas or just St Nicholas Priory was a Benedictine monastery founded in Exeter, England, in 1087. At the Dissolution of the Monasteries the church and chapter house range were pulled down but the domestic buildings were left intact.

spots.name: Bishop's Palace, Exeter
spots.summary: The Bishop's Palace is the residence of the Bishop of Exeter in Exeter, Devon. It is a Grade I Listed building.

spots.name: St Petrock's Church, Exeter

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St Petrock's Church is a small church in the centre of Exeter with an interior described by Nicholas Pevsner as "among the most confusing of any church... in England". The church may have been founded as early as the 6th century, but other sources date it to the 11th century.

spots.name: Spacex

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Spacex was a contemporary art organisation, located in Exeter, between 1974 and 2017. It was founded in 1974 by John Butler as an artists' co-operative. Its programme encompassed installations, performance, photography, sculpture, painting, film and video.

spots.name: Exeter Synagogue

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Exeter Synagogue is a Jewish synagogue, located in Synagogue Place, Mary Arches Street, in the old city of Exeter, Devon, England, in the United Kingdom.

spots.name: St Stephen's Church, Exeter

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: St Stephen's Church is a small church in the centre of Exeter. It has a Saxon crypt but the first mention of the church is in the Domesday Book. Its location was formerly opposite the medieval guildhall. In July 2012 it reopened following a major renovation which cost £1.5 million.

spots.name: Exeter War Memorial
spots.summary: Exeter War Memorial, also known as The Northernhay War Memorial, is a war memorial in Northernhay Gardens in the city of Exeter, Devon. Designed by John Angel, it was erected by public subscription in 1923 and cost over £6,000.

spots.name: Exeter underground passages
spots.summary: The Exeter underground passages were part of the English city of Exeter's medieval water supply system, and are a scheduled monument in the city. The earliest of the tunnels dates from the 13th century. Guided tours of the tunnels are held throughout the year.

spots.name: Equestrian statue of Sir Redvers Buller
spots.summary: An equestrian statue of General Sir Redvers Buller stands at the junction of Hele Road and New North Road, close to Exeter College, Exeter, between St David's Church, Exeter and Bury Meadow Park. It was unveiled in 1905, and the bronze statue is mounted on a plinth of Cornish granite.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Equestrian statue of Sir Redvers Buller

spots.name: Northernhay Gardens
spots.summary: Northernhay Gardens are located in Exeter, Devon, England, on the northern side of Rougemont Castle. They are the oldest public open space in England, being originally laid out in 1612 as a pleasure walk for Exeter residents.

spots.name: St Pancras Church, Exeter

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St Pancras Church is a small church situated in the middle of the Guildhall Shopping Centre in Exeter. The majority of the church dates from the thirteenth century, although the font is eleventh century. The church probably occupies the oldest Christian site in Exeter, and is usually open on weekdays.

spots.name: St Olave's Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St Olave's Church is a parish church located in Exeter, England. The church originated as a private chapel, founded by Lady Gytha, wife of Godwin, Earl of Wessex, and mother of King Harold Godwinson. St Olav's is recorded in the Domesday Book in 1086 AD as church property associated with Battle Abbey in Sussex.

spots.name: George's Chapel, Exeter
spots.summary: George's Chapel or George's Meeting House was built in 1760 as a Presbyterian chapel. It was sold in 1987 and first became an antiques centre before being sold to JD Wetherspoon, who re-opened it as a pub in 2005, preserving many of the original features. It is a grade I listed building.

spots.name: St David's Church, Exeter

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St David's Church, Exeter is a church in Exeter, Devon. It is a Grade I listed building.

spots.name: Rougemont Gardens
spots.summary: Rougemont Gardens is an ornamental open space adjacent to Rougemont Castle in the city of Exeter, Devon, England. It is Grade II listed in the National Register of Historic Parks and Gardens.

spots.name: St Luke's Campus
spots.summary: St Luke's Campus is a small university campus which is part of the University of Exeter. The School of Sport and Health Sciences, the Graduate School of Education, and the Medical School are all based at St Luke's.

spots.name: Royal Devon and Exeter Hospital
spots.summary: The Royal Devon and Exeter Hospital, and with a main site sometimes known as Wonford Hospital, is a large teaching hospital situated in Exeter, Devon, England, and is run by the Royal Devon University Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust.

spots.name: Devon and Exeter Institution

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Devon and Exeter Institution is a subscription library in the City of Exeter, in Devon, United Kingdom, founded in 1813 for "The general diffusion of science, literature and the arts".

spots.name: St Mary Arches Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St Mary Arches Church is a small church in Exeter, Devon, England, which retains many Norman features. It was a place of worship for the Mayor of Exeter and local merchants during the 14th, 15th and 16th centuries.

spots.name: Custom House, Exeter
spots.summary: This Custom House at Exeter was the first in England built for that purpose. It was operated by HM Customs until 1989. Like other former custom houses in the United Kingdom, it now serves as a visitor attraction. It was built in the late 17th-century and has been Grade I listed since 1953.

spots.name: St Margaret's Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St Margaret's Church in Topsham, Devon, is a parish church in the Church of England. It is a Grade II* listed building composed of a 14th-century Gothic tower and a 19th-century Gothic Revival main structure.

spots.name: St Michael and All Angels' Church, Heavitree, Exeter

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of St Michael and All Angels is the main Church of England parish church for the suburb of Heavitree, located in the city of Exeter, Devon. The present building is a large and imposing Gothic Revival structure dating back to the 19th century but there has been a church on the site since Saxon times.
spots.wikipediaTitle: St Michael and All Angels' Church, Heavitree, Exeter

spots.name: St Michael and All Angels Church, Mount Dinham, Exeter

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St Michael and All Angels Church, on Mount Dinham in Exeter is an Anglican church in Devon, England. It is a Grade I listed building. The church is Anglo-Catholic in tradition. The building in is the early Gothic style and was built to the designs of Major Rohde Hawkins, 1867–68. The reredos is by W. D. Caroe, 1899.
spots.wikipediaTitle: St Michael and All Angels Church, Mount Dinham, Exeter

spots.name: Bridge Inn
spots.summary: The Bridge Inn is a Grade II listed public house at Bridge Hill, Topsham in the county of Devon, England. Mentioned as a dwelling in Domesday Book, the building was largely constructed in the 18th century of cob and stone, with a 19th-century brick addition.

spots.name: Streatham Campus
spots.summary: The University of Exeter is a research university in the West Country of England, with its main campus in Exeter, Devon. Its predecessor institutions, St Luke's College, Exeter School of Science, Exeter School of Art, and the Camborne School of Mines were established in 1838, 1855, 1863, and 1888 respectively.

spots.name: St Thomas' Church, Exeter

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St Thomas' Church in Exeter, Devon, is a parish church in the Church of England. It is a Grade I listed building.

spots.name: St James Park
spots.summary: St James Park is a football stadium in Exeter, Devon, England, and is the home of Exeter City Football Club.

spots.name: Cricklepit Mill

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Cricklepit Mill is a visitor centre of the Devon Wildlife Trust, located in Exeter, in Devon, England.

spots.name: Barnfield Theatre
spots.summary: The Barnfield Theatre is a theatre in Exeter, England, located near the centre of the city on Barnfield Road, Southernhay. It was originally built as the Barnfield Hall near the end of the 19th century by Exeter Literary Society, and was converted to a theatre in 1972.

spots.name: Corn Exchange
spots.summary: The Corn Exchange is a market hall and events venue in the Market Street, Exeter, Devon, England. It was designed by the city architect, Harold Rowe and completed in 1960.

spots.name: Devon County Hall
spots.summary: Devon County Hall is a municipal building in Topsham Road, Exeter, Devon, England. The building, which is the headquarters of Devon County Council, is a Grade II* listed building.

spots.name: Northcott Theatre
spots.summary: The Northcott Theatre is a theatre situated on the Streatham Campus of the University of Exeter, Exeter, Devon, England. It opened in 1967 and was run until 2010 by the Northcott Theatre Foundation, when the company ceased operating after a period in administration.

spots.name: Livery Dole

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Livery Dole in Exeter, Devon, is an ancient triangular site between what is today Heavitree Road and Magdalen Road, in the eastern suburbs of Exeter. It was most notoriously used as a place for executions, and has contained an almshouse and chapel since 1591.

spots.name: Exeter Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Exeter Mosque & Cultural Centre is a mosque in the City of Exeter, in Devon, England.

spots.name: Bill Douglas Cinema Museum
spots.summary: The Bill Douglas Cinema Museum is a public museum and an academic research facility on the Streatham Campus of the University of Exeter in England.

spots.name: Topsham Museum
spots.summary: Topsham Museum is a museum in the town of Topsham, Devon, England.

spots.name: Wynard's Hospital
spots.summary: Wynard's Hospital, also known as Wynard's Almshouses or Wynards, is a collection of buildings in Exeter, Devon, originally founded in 1435 as almshousesfor the poor and sick. It is Grade II* listed.

spots.name: Ludwell Valley Park
spots.summary: Ludwell Valley Park is wildlife-focused public park in Exeter, Devon, United Kingdom. The park is owned by Exeter City Council and managed by Devon Wildlife Trust. It has a working farm, with grazing animals, as well as arable fields, in addition to wildflower meadows, woodland, and orchards.

spots.name: Belmont Park
spots.summary: Belmont Park is a public park in Exeter, England. Opened to the public in 1886 as a children's play area, it was subsequently enlarged for the use of the general public.

spots.name: Mary Harris Memorial Chapel of the Holy Trinity

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Mary Harris Memorial Chapel of the Holy Trinity is the Anglican Chaplaincy's chapel on the Streatham Campus of the University of Exeter. It is located at the heart of the campus, beneath Queen's Building and adjacent to the Old Library and the Roborough Building.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Mary Harris Memorial Chapel of the Holy Trinity

spots.name: Westpoint Exeter
spots.summary: Westpoint Exeter is a multi-purpose indoor arena and showground, at Clyst St Mary, near Exeter, England. The capacity of the venue is 7,500 people. It hosts local concerts, fairs and exhibitions. Westpoint is the largest exhibition and entertainment venue in the South West and is located near to Exeter Airport.
